findings: H1 2026 interim results for six months ended 30 June 2026; RNS dated 31 July 2026. Management states performance broadly in line with expectations and full-year guidance remains on track (source: /workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/ITV.L/20260904T164027Z/sources/filings/bodies/d19c5d3b8e0bb46a.txt).

Group H1: total revenue £1,887m vs £1,848m (+2%); external revenue £1,603m vs £1,585m (+1%); group adjusted EBITA £146m flat; adjusted EPS 2.2p vs 1.8p (+22%); statutory PBT £78m vs £67m (+16%); statutory EPS 1.5p vs 1.2p (+25%) (source: /workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/ITV.L/20260904T164027Z/sources/filings/bodies/d19c5d3b8e0bb46a.txt).

ITV Studios H1: total revenue £912m vs £893m (+2%); adjusted EBITA £97m vs £107m (-9%); adjusted EBITA margin 10.6% vs 12.0%; external revenue down 1% on phasing of deliveries; internal revenue up 9%; distribution growth; organic revenue growth +3% vs -1% prior year (source: /workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/ITV.L/20260904T164027Z/sources/filings/bodies/d19c5d3b8e0bb46a.txt).

M&E H1: total revenue £975m vs £955m (+2%); TAR £850m vs £824m (+3%) with Q2 TAR +8% YoY; non-advertising revenue £125m vs £131m (-5%); adjusted EBITA £48m vs £35m (+37%); LHF regulations estimated £20m TAR impact in H1 (source: /workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/ITV.L/20260904T164027Z/sources/filings/bodies/d19c5d3b8e0bb46a.txt).

Digital/ITVX KPIs H1: total M&E digital revenue £307m (+13%); digital advertising £268m (+13%); subscription £26m (+8%); streaming hours 1,418m (+27%, H1 2025 restated from 1,142m); MAUs 17.9m (+10%, H1 2025 restated from 16.4m); UK subscribers 1.1m (+22%); ITVX record H1 viewing up 27% (source: /workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/ITV.L/20260904T164027Z/sources/filings/bodies/d19c5d3b8e0bb46a.txt).

FY26 outlook is for the whole group (Studios and M&E still combined pre-completion): on track for full-year guidance; Studios good revenue growth ahead of market with margin at lower end of 13–15%; M&E strong profitable digital growth via ITVX and Planet V; Q3 2026 TAR expected down ~5% YoY; nine months to September 2026 TAR expected flat YoY (source: /workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/ITV.L/20260904T164027Z/sources/filings/bodies/d19c5d3b8e0bb46a.txt).

Cash and returns: net debt £652m at 30 June 2026 (vs £566m at 31 December 2025); free cash flow £40m H1 (vs £43m); profit-to-cash conversion 63% on 12-month rolling basis; interim dividend 1.7p (~£60m), unchanged, payable November 2026; FY ordinary dividend intention at least 5.0p; £100m share buyback announced 31 July 2026 as early return of ~£950m net cash return on M&E sale completion, expected over 9–12 months (source: /workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/ITV.L/20260904T164027Z/sources/filings/bodies/d19c5d3b8e0bb46a.txt).

Sky M&E sale (announced 6 July 2026): subject to regulatory approval; CMA review started; Public Interest Intervention Notice expected; possible Phase 2 CMA review with completion likely H2 2027 if so; net cash return ~£950m excluding contingent consideration; Sky acquires Channel 3 licences to 2034 with PSB commitments safeguarded; £36m transaction and separation costs in H1 operating exceptional items; FY26 exceptional items guidance raised to ~£95m from ~£55m (source: /workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/ITV.L/20260904T164027Z/sources/filings/bodies/d19c5d3b8e0bb46a.txt).
